info.title: QR Menu Driver API
info.description: The surface consumed by the native Android driver app. Authenticated with a bespoke `DriverToken` bearer (NOT Sanctum, and NOT the POS `PosStaffToken` — a driver must never reach a `/pos/*` route). The token is bound to `driver_id`, not `user_id`, so one login shows the orders of every restaurant the driver is linked to.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Invite → OTP → password. There is no self sign-up (decision 15).

get.summary: Minimum and latest shipped version (public — read before login)
get.description: The app compares `min_version_code` / `latest_version_code` as INTEGERS. Comparing the NAME as a string makes 1.10.0 older than 1.9.0 and locks out a driver who is already on the newest build. The names are for display only.

get.summary: Platform identity — name, logo and accent (public, read before login)
get.description:
The driver app is branded as the PLATFORM, not as any one restaurant (decision 7), and the platform's name and logo are edited in the admin panel — not shipped in the app. A hardcoded logo means a rebrand needs a new APK pushed to every driver's phone; this is read at the login screen instead.

Public, because it is read BEFORE there is a session — the login screen is where it is shown.

The same fields the POS app already reads from `/pos/branding`, served from the same settings. A driver must never reach a `/pos/*` route, so the driver app gets its own path rather than borrowing that one.

Every field is nullable: an unconfigured deployment, or a phone with no connection at the login screen, must still show a usable login screen. The app falls back to the build flavour's own name and mark.

phone.description: Any local form. The server canonicalises with libphonenumber to E.164 and matches `drivers.phone_canonical`, so the driver may type the number the way it was read out to them.

post.summary: Exchange a verified Firebase phone token for the driver's links (public)

firebase_token.description: Firebase Phone Auth ID token; verified server-side.

200.description:
Verified, and SIGNED IN: the returned token is a normal session token, so the driver never has to prove the same phone twice in one sitting. `needs_password` true means this phone has no password yet (first run) or is resetting one — the app then goes straight to `set-password` with this token.

An EMPTY `restaurants` array means the phone is verified but no restaurant has invited it — the app then asks for the invite code, because there is no self sign-up.

post.summary: Choose (or reset) the password, on the session OTP just opened
post.description:
Called straight after `verify-otp`, both on first run and when a driver who forgot their password has just proved the phone again. There is no separate reset endpoint and no reset link: proving the phone IS the reset, which is the only credential a driver reliably has.

The password is what they sign in with from then on, so an SMS is spent once per device rather than on every shift.

password.description: Chosen by the driver, never generated and never sent to them. Minimum six characters — a four-digit code was the earlier design and was changed by the project owner on 2026-09-21, because it is typed from memory for months, not read off an SMS once.

post.description: ONE device session: issuing a token revokes the driver's previous one. The token lives 30 days and renews on use. Rate limited by the `driver-login` limiter (10/min per IP + 5/min per phone+IP) with NO hard per-account lockout — locking by phone alone is a denial of service on a driver whose number is public.

post.summary: Attach this driver to the restaurant that invited them
post.description: The code comes from the restaurant panel over WhatsApp, or is read out loud. A phone that was already invited is linked automatically at verify-otp and never needs this.

get.summary: The driver, their restaurant links and current availability

post.summary: Authorise the private Reverb channel for this driver
post.description: Needed because neither the session cookie nor a POS staff token can authorise a DriverToken holder. Only ever authorises `private-driver.{own driverId}`.

patch.summary: Go available / unavailable (across ALL of the driver's restaurants)
patch.description: Availability is global, not per restaurant (decision 20). The server refuses to go offline mid-trip (`has_active_trip`) and turns availability off by itself only when the branch closes (decision 22) or the location heartbeat has been silent for 3 minutes.

post.summary: Batched location heartbeat (about every 15s while available)
post.description: Points are BATCHED by the client; only the latest is kept as the live position and `last_seen_at` is written to MySQL at most once a minute. Nothing is tracked at all while unavailable.

get.summary: Orders offered to, or claimable by, this driver
get.description:
Scoped to the companies of the driver's ACTIVE links only. Before acceptance the payload deliberately CANNOT carry the customer or the address (decision 23) — see DriverOrderOffered.

An EMPTY `data` is the normal case for most of a shift, so the response also carries `context`: WHY there is nothing, named (decision 47). Only the server knows the radius and the candidate rules, so it must say the reason rather than let the app infer one — a silent empty screen is what makes a driver conclude the app is broken.

get.summary: The driver's active trip (at most one — decision 21)

get.description: Returns the ASSIGNED shape (with customer and address) only when this driver holds the order; otherwise the OFFERED shape. A driver who holds neither gets 404, never 403 — an id is not something to confirm.

post.summary: Acknowledge that the offer was RECEIVED (not accepted)
post.description: The spine of "zero lost offers": no ack within 15s re-sends the push, no ack within 45s re-dispatches to the next candidate. Acking is not accepting and must never be treated as such.
Settled under a row lock: the first driver wins and every other gets 409 `already_claimed`. This is what makes "available to all my restaurants at once" safe.

200.description: The order in its assigned shape — the address and phone appear here.

post.summary: Decline the offer, with a reason
Claim an unassigned order (self-serve assignment modes)
Give the order back before pickup
Handed to the customer, and the cash (if any) collected
post.description:
`cash_collected` is pre-filled by the app with `cash_to_collect` and is editable — but a DIFFERENT amount requires a note, because the gap between what the order said and what the driver holds is exactly what the ledger settles. The driver fee is earned HERE (decision 31).

🔴 `delivery_code` (decision 48) is the customer's proof of receipt, and it is the reason this endpoint can assert a handover rather than merely a driver's claim. The customer reads it off their own order page (or is told it by the cashier who took the call); the driver has to ask for it. It is REQUIRED whenever the order carries one, and the server — never the app — compares. The code is therefore ABSENT from every `/driver/*` response by construction: a code the driver can read is a code that proves nothing.

cash_collected.description: Null for an order already paid. Money is a number, never a string.

delivery_code.description: The four digits the customer holds. Required when the order has a code; null only for an order created before the code existed, or one the restaurant has already waived. Wrong code ⇒ 422 `delivery_code_mismatch`; missing ⇒ 422 `delivery_code_required`. Never echoed back.

post.summary: Report a problem — WITHOUT changing the order status
post.description: Five reasons plus a note. Deliberately does not move the order: a problem is information for the restaurant, not a state transition the driver gets to decide.

post.summary: Compressed trip trail (a point a minute, purged after 30 days)
post.description: Settles the "the driver never arrived" dispute. Not a live tracking feed.

get.summary: The driver's own book, for ONE restaurant
get.description: The book is per (driver × company) and never nets across restaurants (binding rule 2) — which is also what keeps a multi-country driver's currencies apart, since the currency follows the company. `company_id` is therefore required.

get.summary: Settlements already made with the driver

driverToken.description: A `DriverToken` (sha256 at rest) bound to `driver_id`. Not Sanctum, and not interchangeable with the POS staff token.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: A client-generated key, stable across retries of the SAME command. A repeat returns the same 200 body rather than acting twice.

ErrorCode.description: The FROZEN list. A new code is added here AND to all five translations in the same change, or the driver is shown raw English. An unknown code must render a generic translated message and be logged to Sentry.

message.description: ar/en only — for logs and as a fallback, never for branching.

OccurredAt.description: When the event happened ON THE DEVICE. Accepted and clamped between (now − 6h) and now; the server stores BOTH its own time and this one, so a trip finished in a dead zone keeps the real order of its events.

Branding.description: All fields nullable on purpose — see the endpoint description. The app must render a login screen with none of them.

accent_color.description: Hex, e.g. `#B4471F`. Tints the app; the flavour colour is the fallback.

is_active.description: False stops the driver at EVERY restaurant; a link status stops one.

acceptance_rate.description: 0–1. Feeds candidate ordering together with distance (decision 27).

RestaurantLink.description: One restaurant the driver works for. The COUNTRY and the working AREA come from here — the driver never picks either (decisions 45–46), so there is no second source of truth to contradict the invitation.

type.description: `platform` is phase 4 and is not sold yet.

cash_limit.description: Set by the restaurant; 0 or null means no ceiling.

OrderItem.description: A summary WITHOUT prices — the driver is delivering, not selling.

expires_at.description: 45 seconds from dispatch (decision 29). The app counts down to THIS, not 45s from the moment the push happened to arrive.

DriverOrderOffered.description: What a driver may see BEFORE accepting: the area, the distance and the money (decision 23). The customer and the full address are STRUCTURALLY absent — not null, not blanked — so the privacy rule cannot be broken by forgetting to clear a field. Never sent at all: the customer's email, coupons, discounts, online payment detail, staff notes.

currency.description: The ISO code of the branch's currency. A driver may hold links to restaurants in different countries (the ledger is per driver AND per restaurant for exactly that reason), so the app cannot infer one from the device, the account or the previous order — an amount shown without it is a number the driver cannot act on.

cash_to_collect.description: 0 for an order already paid online.

driver_fee.description: The SNAPSHOT stamped at creation (binding rule 3) — never the live zone fee, which a "free delivery" offer zeroes out and with it the driver's pay.

notes.description: The CUSTOMER's note. Staff notes are never sent.

allOf.description: Only ever returned to the driver who holds the order.

requires_delivery_code.description: Whether this order carries a customer delivery code (decision 48) — NOT the code itself, which never crosses this boundary. A boolean leaks nothing: four digits stay unguessable. It exists so the app can ASK for the code up front instead of discovering the requirement from a rejected `delivered`, which would have the driver standing at a door, already refused once, only then turning to the customer to ask. `false` for a pickup order, an order created before the feature, and one the restaurant has waived.

AvailabilityContext.description: Why the available list looks the way it does. `reason` is null whenever `data` is non-empty. This exists because of decision 47: the driver must be told which branches they are linked to and why none of them is offering work, instead of staring at a blank list. It is also the honest answer to "I registered in Saudi Arabia and see nothing" — the cause is almost always distance or a closed branch, and the app can now say so.

has_active_trip.description: One trip at a time (decision 21), so a held order hides the rest.

branches.description: Every branch of every ACTIVE link — named, so the driver can see the restaurant thinks they cover Riyadh while they are in Jeddah.

distance_km.description: Null when the driver's position is unknown (offline, or no fix yet).

search_radius_km.description: The restaurant's own radius (decision 26, 5 km by default).

reason.description: `nothing_pending` is the healthy case: online, in range, a branch is open, there simply is no order yet. It must read differently in the UI from `outside_radius`, which is the driver's own to fix.

cash_on_hand.description: Collected on the restaurant's behalf and not yet handed over.

net.description: Fees earned minus cash held. Positive = the restaurant owes the driver; negative = the driver owes the restaurant.
